sections.normalized_html: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola [MATH: (x+1)^2=8(y-2)?]
sections.readable_text: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola [MATH: (x+1)^2=8(y-2)?]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The standard equation of an upward- or downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at [MATH: (h,k)] is

[MATH: (x-h)^2 = 4p(y-k),]

where [MATH: p] is a constant.

We can rewrite the given equation as [MATH: (x + 1)^{2}|= 4(2)(y − 2).]

It is now clear that our equation is of the standard type with [MATH: p =2.]

Comparing our equation with the standard equation, we can see that we have [MATH: h= -1] and [MATH: k=2.] Therefore, the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola are [MATH: (-1,2).]

sections.normalized_html:
The standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola that has its vertex at [MATH: (h,k)] is

[MATH: (y-k)^2 = 4p(x-h),]

where [MATH: p] is a constant.

We can rewrite the given equation as [MATH: (y-2)^2 = 4\left(\dfrac{2}{4}\right)(x +1),] which simplifies to [MATH: (y-2)^2 = 4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)(x +1),] It is now clear that our equation is of the standard type with [MATH: p=\dfrac{1}{2}.]

Comparing our equation with the standard equation, we can see that we have [MATH: h=-1] and [MATH: k=2.] Therefore, the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola are [MATH: \left(-1,2\right).]
